$comment: Shared entity data for the Cedar policy — the capability/group facts that are true in EVERY
environment. Scope ids and group membership are per-environment and live in pins.<env>.json.
OPEN-SOURCE BUILD. The structure is real; the capability set is an example. A deployment's
capabilities are its own — which external systems an agent may reach is the most
deployment-specific thing in the design — so this ships the shape and a handful of illustrative
entries rather than a real fleet's inventory.
Two things are deliberately NOT here, and both were in the original:
1. HOLDER COUNTS. Each capability carried a count projected over every agent in the fleet. That
is an exposure map — it says which privileged capability is widely held and which is held by
one scope — and it is also a number that is wrong the moment it is written. Derive it when
you need it; do not record it.
2. A COMMS SLUG LIST. A capability group naming the specific outbound actions (send a message,
send mail, upload a file) that a comms approval gate would govern. Ship that once the gate
exists: a declared group with nothing enforcing it describes an intended control rather than
a real one, and the difference matters to anyone reading the policy to find out what is
actually stopped.
$-prefixed keys are ANNOTATION, never data. Every consumer filters on the PREFIX, not the type —
a `$comment` may be a string in one file and an array in another.
Groups that carry AUTHORITY. `baseline` is the ambient set every scope holds without a grant;
it is referenced by the A1 permit in semantics.cedar, so adding a capability here makes it
generally available fleet-wide. Nothing else should be added without a statement to match.
Every capability that can be the resource of a decision, grouped by ORIGIN for review — the
groups above carry authority, this map does not. `tier` records how a capability is reached:
baseline (ambient), grant (a DynamoDB row, per turn), or pin (group membership alone, with no
row involved). A capability absent from this map has no permit, and Cedar's default is deny.
